newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi criticized for defending Andreotti.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi criticized for defending Andreotti.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi drew criticism from politicans and prosecutors on Sunday after defending Giulio Andreotti, seven times premier and now on trial for alleged links to the Mafia.

Prodi said in an interview published in the German newspaper Welt am Sonntag that he could not believe Andreotti, a leading Christian Democrat, protected the mob during his long career as charges against him claim.
Asked if he "could imagine that a man who was seven times prime minister could have supported the Mafia and ordered murders", Prodi answered: "No, it is extremely difficult for me to imagine this,"
"I have faith in justice, but I am losing sleep over this whole affair," said Prodi, who briefly held a post as industry minister in Andreotti's fourth government in 1979.
Andreotti said later on Sunday that he was "pleased with Prodi's words."

"They are part of a tendency that has developed in the last few weeks to give a just political interpretation to this affair," the senator-for-life said in an interview with RAI state television evening news.
But some politicians and prosecutors said Prodi's comments gave an inappropriate political bent to the trial.

"The Andreotti trial has become a political trial, which no longer seeks to uncover a person's penal responsibility but seeks only to bring to justice an era of Italian history," said Rocco Buttiglione, leader of the centre-right CDU party.
"It is shameful," said Buttiglione, whose party rose from the ashes of Andreotti's Christian Democrats.
Anti-Mafia prosecutor Roberto Scarpinato said Prodi's comments could affect the trial negatively.
"Every time there is any type of external, extraneous influence to the trial's procedures, there is a risk of alteration," he told La Repubblica daily.
"It seems difficult to venture an evaluation without knowing. One can offer an opinion, but one has to take into account that one speaks without knowing."
During the trial, which began in 1994, alleged Mafia killers have testified that Andreotti was the mob's political protector from the mid-960s to the mid-1980s.
Andreotti denies the charges, saying they are part of an elaborate Mafia plot to punish him for crackdowns on organised crime by governments he headed.
